facts.statement: Fossil remains of Neogyps have been found in western North America, including the La Brea Tar Pits in southern California.
facts.quote: fossil remains known from western North America, including the La Brea Tar Pits in southern California

facts.statement: The fossil remains of Neogyps date primarily to the Late Pleistocene.
facts.quote: These remains date primarily to the Late Pleistocene

facts.statement: Neogyps lived from the Chibanian to the Late Pleistocene, between 0.21 and 0.0117 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Chibanian to Late Pleistocene (0.21 to 0.0117 million years ago)

facts.statement: Neogyps is classified within the parent group Aegypiinae.
Neogyps belongs to the family Accipitridae.
The type species of the genus Neogyps is Neogyps errans.
Although taxonomically placed among Old World vultures, Neogyps was native to the New World.
facts.quote: Despite its taxonomic placement among Old World vultures, Neogyps was native to the New World

facts.statement: There are six recorded fossil occurrences of Neogyps.

rejected.statement: Neogyps is a member of the class Aves.
Morphological characteristics suggest that Neogyps was closely related to the subfamily Gypaetinae.
rejected.quote: Several morphological characteristics suggest that Neogyps was closely related to the subfamily Gypaetinae
